about: The viewer's filter sets (RENDER_PHYSICS section 2a: the viewer holds the filters, the model holds no palette). Data, sent to /api/render as curves; the model evaluates every published component through them (S38, D113 option (a)). Channels are listed red, green, blue: the display channel each filter is drawn in. Wavelengths in angstroms, in air. Every curve here is [inferred]: an analytic stand-in stated as such, no instrument's measured transmission. tests/test_render.py reads this file, so the gate runs on the curves the viewer sends.

rgb.label: RGB
rgb.about: Broadband: three Gaussians at the reference wavelengths and FWHMs of the Bessell R, V and B passbands the isochrone table's magnitudes are in, the same numbers as the model's own band definitions (photometry.PASSBANDS) [verified: SVO Filter Profile Service, Generic/Bessell.R, .V, .B, read at S38]. The Gaussian shape is [inferred]. Until the S38 second cut these were recalled numbers (6407/1580, 5448/840, 4361/890 A).

sho.label: SHO
sho.about: Narrowband false colour, the 'Hubble palette': [S II] 6716/6731 in red, Halpha 6563 in green, [O III] 5007 in blue. Boxes 30 A wide at the lines' air wavelengths [inferred: a flat-topped interference filter of a commonly sold width]; the [S II] box is centred between the doublet and holds both.

hoo.label: HOO
hoo.about: Bicolour false colour: Halpha in red, [O III] in green and in blue. The same 30 A boxes as SHO [inferred].

ir.label: IR
ir.about: The infrared set (S39, BUILD_II V2), sent to /api/render to read the dust's thermal emission and the energy balance, and not drawn: a 6500 K white point makes no sense of a far-infrared channel, and a white per channel is a display choice not yet made. Four boxes: a box named TIR on the wire that is Sanders & Mirabel 1996's 8 to 1000 micron L_IR, not Dale & Helou 2002's 3 to 1100 micron TIR ('we refer to this as the total-infrared or TIR luminosity', Kennicutt & Evans 2012 [verified: arXiv:1204.3552, definitions, read at S43 (Audit IV A4-6)]; the short edge is worth 5e-7 of the dust's emission here, so the box's name stays for the viewer's contract and the label says which), wide enough to hold the modified blackbody's peak (about 130 microns at 20 K) and all but 0.068% of the default galaxy's dust emission (what lies beyond 1 mm, from its coldest outer dust, tests/test_render.py); and K, H, J at the reference wavelengths of the Bessell & Brett passbands the isochrone table's J H K magnitudes are in, each box as wide as the passband's FWHM, the same numbers as the model's own band definitions (photometry.PASSBANDS) [verified: SVO Filter Profile Service, Generic/Bessell_JHKLM.J, .H, .K, read at S38]. The box shapes are [inferred].

white.about: The tone map's white point: each channel is divided by the model's response of a blackbody at this temperature per unit light, so a 6500 K source draws white in every set [inferred: near sRGB's D65 white, a display choice, not a physical constant].
